to initiate into the mysteries (so chiefly in cl.; LXX, III Mac 2:30); hence, to instruct: pass., (RV, I have learned the secret).†

G3437.as:
* μομφή, ῆς, ἡ (< μέμφομαι), poët. form of μέμψις,
blame, complaint: .†

G3401.as:
μιμέομαι, -οῦμαι (< μῖμος, a mimic, an actor), [in LXX: Ps 30 (31):6, Wi 4:2 15:9, IV Mac 9:23 13:9*;]
to imitate: , , , .†

G3454.as:
** μῦθος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Wi 17:4 A, Si 20:19*;]
1. speech, conversation.
2.
(a) a story, narrative (Hom.);
(b) later, opp. to λόγος (a true narrative) = Lat. fabula, a myth, fable, fiction: , , , .†
SYN.: λόγος, q.v.

G3443.as:
** μονόω, -ῶ (< μόνος), [in Aq.: Ge 49:6;]
to leave alone, forsake: of a childless widow, pf. ptcp. pass., .†

G3405.as:
*† μισθαποδοσία, -ας, ἡ (< μισθός, ἀποδίδωμι; cl. μισθοδοσία),
payment of wages, recompense; meton.,
(a) of reward: ;
(b) of punishment: .†

G3452.as:
μυελός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: Ge 45:18 (חֵלֶב), Jb 21:24 (מֹחַ) Jb 33:24*;]
marrow: .†

G3406.as:
*† μισθ-απο-δότης, -ου, ὁ, (v. supr.),
one who pays wages; meton., a rewarder: .†

G3468.as:
μώλωψ, -ωπος, ὁ, [in LXX for חַבּוּרָה, Ex 21:25, al.;]
a bruise, wound from a stripe: (LXX) (Arist., Plut., al.).†

G3467.as:
*† μυ-ωπάζω (< μύωψ, closing the eyes, short-sighted; < μύω, ὤψ),
to be short-sighted: (R, mg., closing his eyes; v. ICC, in l.).†

G3420.as:
μνήμη, -ης, ἡ (< μνάομαι), [in LXX for זֵכֶר, זִכָּרוֹן;]
memory, remembrance, mention: μ. ποιεῖσθαι, c. gen., to remember, (but in cl., π., μ. π. more freq. = to make mention, and so perh. here, cf. Mayor, in l.; and for ex. from π., v. Zorell, s.v.).†
SYN.: μνεία, q.v.

G3470.as:
μῶμος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX, of physical blemishes: Le 21:17 ff., De 15:21, Ca 4:7, al. (מוּם); of mental defect, Si 20:24, al.;]
1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace.
2. In LXX, perh. because of resemblance to מוּםpossible misspelling of מאוּם, a physical blemish (cf. ἄμωμος, , and v. Hort., in l.); metaph., of licentious persons, .†

G3413.as:
Μιχαήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. מִיכָאֵל, who like God?),
Michael, the Archangel (cf. Da 12:1): , .†

G3455.as:
** μυκάομαι, -ῶμαι, in cl. chiefly poët., [in Sm.: Jb 6:5*;]
prop., of oxen (onomatop.), to low, bellow; of a lion, to roar: .†

G3451.as:
μουσικός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX: Ge 31:27, Ez 26:13 (שִׁיר), Da LXX TH 3:5 ff. (זְמָר), Si 22:6, al.;]
skilled in the arts, esp. in music; as subst., ὁ μ., a minstrel, musician: .†
